skill.name: skill-share
skill.description: Creates structured Claude skill packages, validates their metadata, and shares approved skill details with team Slack channels through Rube.
skill.summary: Create, validate, package, and announce reusable Claude skills.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static external-command finding is a false positive caused by a fenced Markdown example, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. However, the workflow proposes automatic Slack posting and direct file links without requiring user confirmation, which may disclose internal skill information.

remediation.issue: Slack announcements may expose skill metadata or file links without a final user review.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of the destination channel and exact message before every Slack post.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 59-66 are a fenced Markdown usage example. They contain no Ruby backtick expression, shell command, or executable code.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic External Sharing Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs automatic Slack posting of skill metadata and direct file links, but it does not require confirmation of the message or destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated feature explicitly sends information to Slack and provides direct file links. No approval or content-review step is specified.

content.value_statement: Teams often build skills without consistent structure, validation, or visibility. This skill organizes creation and packaging, then prepares Slack announcements through Rube.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a skill directory with a SKILL.md file.
Defines standard scripts, references, and assets directories.
Checks naming conventions and required metadata before packaging.
Packages skill files into a distributable archive.
Prepares Slack announcements with skill names, descriptions, summaries, and links.
Uses named Rube actions to find channels and post Slack messages.
limitations: The skill contains guidance only and includes no creation or validation scripts.
Slack sharing requires a configured Rube connection and an accessible destination channel.
File creation and packaging require local write access.
The workflow does not define safeguards for confidential content or destination approval.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: Create a consistent skill package with required metadata and directories before internal distribution.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reusable Automations
use_cases.description: Package a documented skill for colleagues who use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Announce New Skills
use_cases.description: Prepare a concise Slack announcement so teammates can discover a newly packaged skill.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named [name] for [purpose]. Include a clear SKILL.md file and the standard directory structure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new skill from a simple requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Skill Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Check its name, frontmatter, required metadata, directories, and packaging readiness. List each issue before making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an existing skill before distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Package and Draft an Announcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate and package the skill at [path]. Draft a Slack announcement for [channel], but wait for my approval before posting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a validated archive and a controlled team announcement.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Reviewed Team Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [path] for confidential content, validate its structure, and prepare a package. Show the archive contents and Slack message for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate an advanced release with content and destination review.

output_examples.input: Create a skill named release-notes for drafting product updates.
output_examples.output: Created the release-notes skill structure with metadata and standard directories. Validation found no missing required fields.

output_examples.input: Package the onboarding-checklist skill and prepare a Slack announcement.
output_examples.output: The skill is ready for packaging. Proposed announcement: New Skill Created: onboarding-checklist, a reusable onboarding checklist for team workflows.

output_examples.input: Check the data-cleanup skill before sharing it.
output: Validation result: the skill name follows the required convention.
The description is present, but the license metadata is missing.
Slack sharing remains pending until the channel and message are approved.

best_practices: Review generated metadata and archive contents before distribution.
Confirm the Slack channel and exact announcement before posting.
Remove secrets, private links, and confidential examples from shared packages.
anti_patterns: Do not announce a skill before validation completes.
Do not share local file links that teammates cannot access.
Do not post confidential skill content to broad Slack channels.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides creation of a structured skill directory, metadata, supporting folders, and a distributable package.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The published skill contains workflow guidance but no bundled creation, validation, or packaging scripts.

faq.question: Is Slack required?
faq.answer: Slack is required only for announcements. Skill creation and packaging can be planned without Slack.

faq.question: What is Rube used for?
faq.answer: Rube provides actions for finding Slack channels and sending standard or rich messages.

faq.question: Can it validate any skill?
faq.answer: It describes checks for SKILL.md metadata and naming. It does not provide a complete validator implementation.

faq.question: How should sensitive skills be shared?
faq.answer: Review package contents, remove secrets, confirm access controls, and approve the destination channel before posting.
